name: Chimaerasuchus
sum: Chimaerasuchus is a short-snouted crocodyliform with multicusped teeth from the Early Cretaceous Wulong Formation of China, likely herbivorous.
wsnote: The skull is about 135 mm long with a snout of about 65 mm; no body length is given.
holotype: Not stated in the sources consulted for this draft; found in the 1960s and identified as a crocodyliform in 1995.
material: Skull material; once thought to be a multituberculate mammal.
biology: Marked heterodonty and multicusped teeth suggest it was herbivorous, and four teeth at the snout tip gave it a bucktoothed look.
author: Wu et al. 1995

sources.text: X.-C. Wu, H.-D. Sues, and A. Sun. 1995. A plant-eating crocodyliform reptile from the Cretaceous of China. Nature 376:678-680
